terminalup.name: TerminalUp
terminalup.what: One account that routes orders to sportsbooks, betting exchanges and prediction markets. The board shows the best available price across every connected venue, with the size available at that price, and the order goes to whichever venue is best.
terminalup.fit: Traders moving size who want the best price and the deepest liquidity without holding a dozen accounts.
terminalup.pricing: 0.5% commission per trade. On a win, 0.5% of profit; on a loss, 0.5% of the amount risked. No subscription, no data fee, no deposit fee. Can go down to 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts.
terminalup.custody: You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it.
terminalup.lacks: Not for small bankrolls: the minimum is $10,000. No bonuses or promotions, because TerminalUp is not a bookmaker and never takes a position against you.
terminalup.not: Not a sportsbook. Not an odds-screen subscription. TerminalUp does not set lines or hold the other side of a trade.

oddsjam.name: OddsJam
oddsjam.what: A subscription screen that compares prices across sportsbooks and flags positive expected value and arbitrage opportunities. You place every bet yourself at each book.
oddsjam.fit: Recreational and semi-professional bettors who hold several sportsbook accounts and want to shop lines.
oddsjam.lacks: No execution. It tells you where the price is; you still log in to each book and place the bet by hand, and the price may be gone by then.

unabated.name: Unabated
unabated.type: Odds screen and pricing tools for sharp bettors
unabated.what: A professional-grade odds screen with a market-based fair line, player prop pricing and a bet tracker. Built by bettors with a quant background. No execution.
unabated.fit: Serious bettors who price markets themselves and want a clean screen and a fair line to compare against.
unabated.lacks: No routing or execution. Like every screen, it stops at the moment you need to place the bet.

betstamp.name: Betstamp
betstamp.what: A free odds screen with line shopping across books and a tracker for your bets. Good for finding the best price on a slate and logging what you did.
betstamp.fit: Bettors who want a free screen and a tracker in one place.
betstamp.lacks: No execution, and the free data is shallower than the paid screens.

pinnacle.name: Pinnacle
pinnacle.what: The reference book for sharp prices: low margins, high limits and a long-standing policy of welcoming winning players. Not available to US residents directly.
pinnacle.fit: Professionals who want to bet into a low-margin book with real limits.
pinnacle.pricing: Built into the price: Pinnacle's margin is among the lowest of any book.
pinnacle.lacks: Not accessible from the US, and even at Pinnacle one book is one book: no price comparison and no routing.

circa.name: Circa Sports
circa.what: The Las Vegas book that built its name on taking sharp action at real limits, with a mobile app in a handful of states.
circa.fit: US bettors in Circa's states who want a book that will not run from a winner.
circa.pricing: Built into the price: low margins, no subscription.
circa.lacks: Available in a few states, and it is still one book with one price.

novig.name: Novig
novig.what: A US exchange where users trade against each other instead of a house. Prices come from the order book, and the operator does not take positions.
novig.fit: US bettors in supported states who want exchange prices without a bookmaker's margin.
novig.lacks: One book of liquidity. The price is Novig's price, and on a quiet market the best price may be sitting at another venue.

prophetx.name: ProphetX
prophetx.what: A US sports betting exchange with an order book, where you can post your own price or take one that is already there.
prophetx.fit: Exchange bettors in supported states who want to make markets as well as take them.
prophetx.lacks: Liquidity is limited to its own book, and availability depends on state.

sporttrade.name: Sporttrade
sporttrade.what: A regulated US exchange where sports outcomes trade like contracts from 0 to 100, with an order book and the ability to sell a position before the game ends.
sporttrade.fit: Bettors in supported states who think in prices and want to trade in and out of positions.
sporttrade.lacks: A single pool of liquidity, and only in the states where it is licensed.

betfair.name: Betfair Exchange
betfair.what: The largest betting exchange in the world, where backers and layers trade against each other and the operator charges commission on net winnings.
betfair.fit: Bettors outside the US who want deep exchange liquidity on major sports and racing.
betfair.pricing: Commission on net winnings on a market; the base rate varies by market and account.
betfair.lacks: Not available in the US, and one exchange is still one price.

matchbook.name: Matchbook
matchbook.what: A betting exchange with low commission and a strong US-sports book, popular with traders outside the US.
matchbook.fit: Non-US exchange traders who want lower commission than the biggest exchange.
matchbook.lacks: Thinner liquidity than Betfair on many markets, and not available in the US.

kalshi.name: Kalshi
kalshi.what: A CFTC-regulated exchange for event contracts, including sports outcomes, where each contract pays $1 if the event happens. Legal across the US.
kalshi.fit: US traders who want a regulated, nationwide venue for sports and event contracts.
kalshi.pricing: Trading fees per contract, charged on the trade.
kalshi.lacks: One order book. Sports liquidity varies by market, and the price on Kalshi is not always the best price available.

polymarket.name: Polymarket
polymarket.what: One of the two largest prediction markets, with a CFTC-regulated US app and an international on-chain market. Deep books on big events and growing sports coverage.
polymarket.fit: Traders comfortable with crypto rails who want the deepest prediction-market liquidity.
polymarket.pricing: Low or no trading fees on most markets.
polymarket.lacks: US access has been restricted historically, and sports books are thinner than its political markets.

predictfun.name: predict.fun
predictfun.what: An on-chain prediction market with sports and event contracts.
predictfun.fit: Crypto-native traders who want another venue for event contracts.
predictfun.lacks: Smaller books than the two largest prediction markets.

sxbet.name: SX Bet
sxbet.what: A blockchain-based peer-to-peer betting exchange where users trade sports outcomes on an order book.
sxbet.fit: Crypto-native bettors who want exchange pricing without a house.
sxbet.lacks: Liquidity varies by market and the crypto rails are a barrier for many.

dratings.name: Action Network
dratings.what: Odds comparison, public betting data and a tracker, aimed at the mainstream bettor.
dratings.fit: Casual bettors who want odds and context in one app.
dratings.lacks: Not a sharp tool: no execution, and shallow on exchanges and prediction markets.

oddschecker.name: Oddschecker
oddschecker.what: The best-known odds comparison site, UK-born, listing bookmaker prices side by side with links out to each book. Free, funded by affiliate commissions.
oddschecker.fit: Casual bettors who want a quick look at which book has the best price on a popular market.
oddschecker.lacks: Bookmaker-only, affiliate-driven, and read-only; you place the bet at the book.

oddsportal.name: OddsPortal
oddsportal.what: A global odds comparison site with a large archive of historical odds, used as much for research as for shopping.
oddsportal.fit: Bettors and researchers who want to see how lines moved and compare books across many countries.
oddsportal.lacks: Read-only, bookmaker-focused, and slower to update than a professional screen.

donbest.name: Don Best
donbest.what: The long-running odds screen used in sportsbooks and by professionals, showing line movement across books in real time.
donbest.fit: Professionals who want the classic multi-book screen with line history.
donbest.lacks: A screen, not a venue: no execution, and light on exchanges and prediction markets.

spotodds.name: SpotOdds
spotodds.what: A real-time odds screen built for sharps, with fast line-move alerts across many books and exchanges.
spotodds.fit: Sharp bettors who care about seeing the move first.
spotodds.lacks: No execution; you still bet at the book or exchange.

rebelbetting.name: RebelBetting
rebelbetting.what: Long-running subscription software that scans bookmakers for arbitrage and value bets and shows the stakes to place at each book.
rebelbetting.fit: Bettors who want a dedicated arb and value scanner across many bookmakers.
rebelbetting.lacks: Bookmaker-centric, no execution, and the bets still have to be placed by hand at each book before the window closes.

betburger.name: BetBurger
betburger.what: A subscription scanner that surfaces arbitrage and value opportunities across a long list of bookmakers and some exchanges.
betburger.fit: Arb bettors who want wide bookmaker coverage and fast alerts.
betburger.lacks: No execution; bookmaker limits still apply; you place every leg yourself.

theoddsapi.name: The Odds API
theoddsapi.what: A simple REST API returning odds from a long list of sportsbooks, priced by request volume.
theoddsapi.fit: Developers who need bookmaker odds in JSON quickly and cheaply.
theoddsapi.pricing: Free tier, then monthly plans by request volume.
theoddsapi.lacks: Polled snapshots rather than a live stream, and no exchange or prediction-market depth.

opticodds.name: OpticOdds
opticodds.what: A commercial odds feed covering many sportsbooks with real-time delivery, used by odds platforms and operators.
opticodds.fit: Businesses that need a licensed, real-time bookmaker feed.
opticodds.lacks: Bookmaker-centric: thin on exchange depth and no sense of what size is available.

sportradar.name: Sportradar
sportradar.what: The incumbent data company for sports leagues and operators, with odds feeds among many products.
sportradar.fit: Operators and media companies buying data at scale.
sportradar.lacks: Not built for a developer with a credit card, and not an executable-price feed.

betfair_api.name: Betfair Exchange API
betfair_api.what: Betfair's developer API: streaming market data and order placement for the Betfair Exchange, with a long history of third-party tools built on it.
betfair_api.fit: Developers building trading tools on the deepest single exchange.
betfair_api.pricing: Free with an app key; some data tiers are charged.
betfair_api.lacks: One exchange's book only, and Betfair does not serve the US.

kalshi_api.name: Kalshi API
kalshi_api.what: Kalshi's trading API: market data, order books and order placement for its regulated event contracts, with WebSocket feeds.
kalshi_api.fit: Developers building on a regulated US event-contract exchange.
kalshi_api.pricing: Free API access; trading fees apply to trades.
kalshi_api.lacks: One venue's book, and sports depth varies by market.

terminalup_odds_api.name: TerminalUp Odds API
terminalup_odds_api.what: REST, Server-Sent Events and WebSocket delivery of the best fee-adjusted price per outcome across TerminalUp's connected venues, with the size available at that price, a bounded ladder, and an honest status for every market. Sandbox keys for building before a license.
terminalup_odds_api.fit: Developers and odds platforms that need a price someone can actually take, with depth, rather than a list of bookmaker quotes.
terminalup_odds_api.pricing: Keys issued per partner; sandbox free.
terminalup_odds_api.lacks: Current state only, no history endpoint. Coverage follows TerminalUp's licensed venues.

pikkit.name: Pikkit
pikkit.what: A free tracker that syncs bets automatically from US sportsbooks, so the record is complete without typing anything in. Shows profit by sport, book and bet type.
pikkit.fit: Bettors on mainstream US books who want a verified record with no effort.
pikkit.lacks: No execution and no odds screen; it records what you did elsewhere.

juicereel.name: Juice Reel
juicereel.what: Syncs bets from a long list of sportsbooks and DFS sites, tracks CLV and results, and runs a marketplace where handicappers' records are verified from their synced accounts. Adds AI picks and matchup notes.
juicereel.fit: Bettors who want automatic tracking plus verified records of other people's picks.
juicereel.pricing: Free to download, with in-app purchases and paid picks.
juicereel.lacks: The picks marketplace and AI features sit on top of the tracker, so the app does a lot at once.

rithmm.name: Rithmm
rithmm.what: Lets a bettor build and tune predictive models for major US sports without code, then surfaces picks and props from the model against current lines.
rithmm.fit: Bettors who want their own model rather than someone else's picks.
rithmm.pricing: Paid subscription, tiered by sport and features.
rithmm.lacks: Model output is only as good as its inputs, and there is no execution or price routing.

leansai.name: Leans.ai
leansai.what: Publishes model-driven picks across the major leagues, with the team describing a background in building computer models for sports.
leansai.fit: Bettors who want a daily card from a model and will shop the price themselves.
leansai.lacks: A picks feed, not a tool; you still need a venue and a price.

dimers.name: Dimers
dimers.what: Data-driven game and prop predictions across US sports, with best-bet tools, projections and odds, part free and part behind Dimers Pro.
dimers.fit: Bettors who want model predictions and a browse-everything layout.
dimers.pricing: Free tier; Dimers Pro subscription for the full toolset.
dimers.lacks: Predictions are shown against book prices, but nothing is placed from the site.

outlier.name: Outlier
outlier.what: Player-prop research with hit rates, trends and projections against the lines, aimed at prop bettors who want the numbers behind a market.
outlier.fit: Prop bettors who research each line.
outlier.pricing: Free tier with a paid Pro plan.

smarkets.name: Smarkets
smarkets.what: A UK-licensed betting exchange with a flat commission on net winnings and prices set by other users.
smarkets.fit: Non-US bettors who want a low-commission exchange alongside Betfair.
smarkets.lacks: Not available to US residents; thinner than Betfair on most markets.

robinhood_pm.name: Robinhood Prediction Markets
robinhood_pm.type: Prediction markets inside a brokerage app
robinhood_pm.what: Event contracts on sports, politics and economics offered inside the Robinhood app through a CFTC-registered exchange partner.
robinhood_pm.fit: People who already hold a Robinhood account and want event contracts without another app.
robinhood_pm.pricing: A per-contract fee on each trade; see the app for the current schedule.
robinhood_pm.lacks: A curated subset of markets, and no cross-venue pricing.

cryptocom_pm.name: Crypto.com Sports
cryptocom_pm.what: Sports event contracts inside the Crypto.com app, offered through its CFTC-registered derivatives exchange.
cryptocom_pm.fit: Crypto.com users who want sports contracts in the same app.
cryptocom_pm.lacks: One venue's liquidity and a narrower market list than the dedicated exchanges.

predictit.name: PredictIt
predictit.what: The long-running US political prediction market, with contracts on elections and government, operated under CFTC permissions.
predictit.fit: People who trade politics rather than sports.
predictit.pricing: Fees on profits and withdrawals; see the site.
predictit.lacks: No sports markets and position limits per contract.

manifold.name: Manifold
manifold.what: A user-created prediction market that runs on play money, with thousands of questions and a forecasting community.
manifold.fit: Learning how markets price questions without staking real money.
manifold.lacks: No real money, so prices are less disciplined than on a cash market.

metaculus.name: Metaculus
metaculus.what: A reputation-based forecasting site on science, technology and world events. No money changes hands; forecasters are scored on accuracy.
metaculus.fit: Reading aggregated forecasts on long-horizon questions.
metaculus.lacks: Not a market and nothing to trade.

underdog.name: Underdog
underdog.type: US sports app with event contracts
underdog.what: A US sports app offering predictions, pick'em and season-long fantasy, with event contracts traded on Underdog Exchange.
underdog.fit: People who want a consumer sports app for predictions and fantasy.

rothera.name: Rothera
rothera.type: Exchange and clearing venue for event contracts
rothera.what: An exchange and clearing venue for event contracts, built for institutions and intermediaries.
rothera.fit: Institutions that need a venue and clearing partner for event contracts.

pred.name: Pred
pred.what: A sports prediction exchange where outcomes trade as contracts priced in cents.
pred.fit: Traders who want sports contracts on one exchange.

limitless.name: Limitless
limitless.what: A prediction market covering crypto, sports, esports, finance and politics.
limitless.fit: Traders who want its markets on their own.
